== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|Territories are distinct worlds or realms that exist apart from the [[Unnamed World]]. Traditionally, there were nine original Territories that encompass all natural powers, though a tenth, [[Elysia]], was later established to represent human virtues. While most Territories are accessed intentionally by [[Travelers]] through [[Gates]] to acquire specific powers or allies, some may be entered unexpectedly. A Territory can also manifest as a single structure, such as a house that contains an entire world within its walls. These realms are closely linked to [[Incarnations]], individuals who have lost control and become embodiments of their Territory's specific nature. An [[Incarnation]]'s presence can warp the surrounding reality to mirror their realm, though staying too long in a Territory can cause an [[Incarnation]] to be absorbed into its fabric. While most Territories are separate locations, [[Valinhall]] is a unique case; it was formed by a [[Founder]] who bound together shards of an older world, and its primary purpose is to equip its [[Travelers]] for combat against those from other Territories. Because of the metaphysical distance between these realms, a [[Traveler]]'s full power cannot be utilized when they are within another's Territory.}}

== House of Blades ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|A Territory is a power summoned by a [[Traveler]] from another location, accessible through the use of a Gate. These realms can manifest as anything from a moon-lit wasteland to a house that holds an entire world within its walls. Within these spaces, normal physical laws barely hold sway and time flows differently, as each area is governed by its own unique rules and restrictions. While they are places where magical events are expected to occur, a [[Traveler]] can call upon their Territory using a pattern or respond to a mental call. [[Simon]] possesses a Territory containing a [[Damascan]] family, which he accessed through cool breath and [[liquid steel]], while [[Alin]] has utilized the borrowed power of his own Territory to reinforce a shield.}}

== The Crimson Vault ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|A Territory is a specific type of domain or location that encompasses all the powers of nature. [[Kai]] possesses the ability to reach through his [[sword]] to access his own Territory, while [[Simon]] has been observed within his. Within these spaces, [[Simon]] is able to draw both speed and strength, though the [[frozen horn]] loses its functionality once inside. While [[Naraka Traveler|Naraka Travelers]] may eventually learn to maintain their composure and stay cool within such a domain, the mere presence of a Territory serves to keep an [[Incarnation]] in check.}}

== City of Light ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|A Territory serves as a realm that grants its possessor supernatural vision. While [[Alin]] possesses the ability to transmit energy directly to his own Territory, [[Ilana]] only becomes aware of such a space upon falling into one. Within these realms, [[Incarnations]] may pursue personal objectives by exploiting foreign [[Travelers]]. The history of certain Territories includes the sealing of [[Indirial]], while [[Simon]] remains bound to his by a chain and exists in a state of debt to it.}}

<div class="wv-facts mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"><div class="wv-facts-head mw-collapsible-toggle">Sourced facts <span class="wv-facts-count">7</span></div>

<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|[[Ilana]] recognizes a [[Territory]] when she falls into one.<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c15">''City of Light'', chapter 15</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-03-city-of-light|[[Incarnations]] existing within Territories can advance their own goals at the expense of foreign [[Travelers]].<ref name="tg-03-city-of-light-c18">''City of Light'', chapter 18</ref>}}</li>
